steps.prompt: What does the word that do here?
options: It joins the sentence to a second part which describes the thing.
It asks a question about the thing the sentence names.
It makes the sentence negative instead of positive.
steps.answer: It joins the sentence to a second part which describes the thing.
steps.why: A defining relative clause tells you which thing or person we mean. Without it the sentence is incomplete.

steps.title: who / which / that / where
steps.html:
Use it forExample
who — a personThe neighbour who fixes electronics.
which — a thingThe dish which has not worked since 2019.
that — a person or a thingThe chest of drawers that her father made.
where — a placeThe room where the guests sleep.

The relative word comes straight after the noun it describes: the thing which hangs above the basin.

That can replace who and which in this kind of clause. It cannot replace where.

Do not repeat the noun with a pronoun: say the man who lives here, not the man who he lives here.

This is how you name a thing when the word has gone: It’s the thing that you clean the floor with.

You will use exactly this pattern again in Unit 5, Lesson 15, to explain a word you don’t know.

steps.title: You are going to read about one room in a flat.
steps.sub: Which of these do you think are in it? There is no wrong answer here.

steps.title: The room that tells you everything
steps.html:
Every object in the room has a story.

Reading

Amina rents out one room in her flat, and the people who stay there always ask about the same objects.

The first is the thing which hangs above the wash basin — an old mirror with a wooden frame. It was her grandmother’s, and it is the only object in the flat that she would never sell.

Next to the bed there is a chest of drawers that her father made. The drawers are heavy and one of them does not close, but every guest who opens it finds the same thing inside: a box of candles. There are no lamps in the room where Amina’s guests sleep, and in winter the electricity sometimes stops for an hour.

The kitchen is the place where visitors are most surprised. There is a microwave oven, but there is only one pan, and the cloth that hangs by the tap is older than most of the guests. “People who come from big cities think a kitchen needs twenty things,” Amina says. “It needs three.”

On the balcony there is a satellite dish which has not worked since 2019. Amina keeps it because a neighbour who fixes electronics has promised to look at it. The rug on the floor, the towels in the wardrobe, the duvet on the bed — none of them is new, and none of them is strange to anyone who grew up here.

“The flat is not modern,” she says. “But everything in it is something that somebody in my family chose.”

The violet words are the relative words. Look at the noun that comes just before each one.

steps.title: Choose the best answer.
steps.prompt: What is the main idea of the text?
options: The objects in Amina’s room are old but each one was chosen by her family.
Amina wants to sell her flat and buy modern furniture for the new one.
Amina’s guests complain about the kitchen and about the broken drawer.
steps.answer: The objects in Amina’s room are old but each one was chosen by her family.
steps.why: The last line: “everything in it is something that somebody in my family chose”.

There are no lamps in the room where Amina’s guests sleep, and in winter the electricity sometimes stops for an hour.

The kitchen is the place where visitors are most surprised. There is a microwave oven, but there is only one pan, and the cloth that hangs by the tap is older than most of the guests. “People who come from big cities think a kitchen needs twenty things,” Amina says. “It needs three.”

On the balcony there is a satellite dish which has not worked since 2019. Amina keeps it because a neighbour who fixes electronics has promised to look at it. The rug on the floor, the towels in the wardrobe, the duvet on the bed — none of them is new, and none of them is strange to anyone who grew up here.

“The flat is not modern,” she says. “But everything in it is something that somebody in my family chose.”

The violet words are the relative words. Look at the noun that comes just before each one.
